change.title: 6 changes: @google/generative-ai (npm) is deprecated and reaches end of life; migrate to @google/genai and more

source.quote: All support for this repository (including bug fixes) will permanently end on **November 30, 2025**.

tasks.reasoning:
This one task covers all 6 gemini changes that affect this repo. Handle every one of them in this single change set, prove each with your test, and say in finish which you changed and which needed no change.

1. @google/generative-ai (npm) is deprecated and reaches end of life; migrate to @google/genai (sdk-major, effective 2025-11-30)
   Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/generative-ai-js/HEAD/README.md
   Quote: All support for this repository (including bug fixes) will permanently end on **November 30, 2025**.
   Affects: versions: <=0.24.1; sdk: @google/generative-ai
   Call sites: app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:56 (Calls getGenerativeModel through @google/generative-ai, which is end of life.); lib/ai-advanced-utils.ts:4 (Same deprecated SDK, getGenerativeModel with gemini-2.0-flash.); lib/ai-client.ts:87 (Same deprecated SDK, getGenerativeModel with generationConfig. The migration must map generationConfig to the @google/genai config shape.); lib/ai-utils.ts:4 (Same deprecated SDK, getGenerativeModel with gemini-2.0-flash.)
   Why it applies: The repo pins @google/generative-ai 0.24.1, which is inside the affected range (<=0.24.1). Support for it ended on 2025-11-30, so there will be no more fixes or new model support. The fix is to migrate to @google/genai: replace getGenerativeModel with ai.models.generateContent, move generationConfig into config, and update how responses are read. The repo only uses generateContent-style calls, so the @google/genai 0.x, 1.x and 2.0 breaking changes (Interactions, Lyria, early contents types) do not add edits. Raw HTTP in usage 4 is not touched by this SDK move. The gemini-2.0-flash shutdown is a separate model-string edit.

2. gemini-2.0-flash and flash-lite models shut down June 1 2026 (model-retirement, effective 2026-06-01)
   Source: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/changelog.md.txt
   Quote: The following Gemini 2.0 models are now [shut down](/docs/deprecations):
   Affects: operations: gemini-2.0-flash, gemini-2.0-flash-001, gemini-2.0-flash-lite, gemini-2.0-flash-lite-001
   Call sites: app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:56 (Model is hard-coded to gemini-2.0-flash, which is shut down and will fail.); lib/ai-advanced-utils.ts:4 (Model is gemini-2.0-flash.); lib/ai-utils.ts:4 (Model is gemini-2.0-flash.); lib/ai-client.ts:87 (The model name is not resolved by the scan. It may be gemini-2.0-flash or a -lite variant, or come from config or an env var. Check it.); app/api/hackathon/match-teams/route.ts:135 (Raw HTTP call with a runtime-built URL. The model is unknown, so check whether it names a gemini-2.0-flash or -lite model. Uncertain.)
   Why it applies: The pinned model is gemini-2.0-flash at three call sites, and Google has shut down gemini-2.0-flash and the flash-lite variants. Chat and AI utility features will return errors. Replace the model with a currently supported one, and do not choose gemini-2.5-flash or gemini-2.5-pro, which are scheduled to reroute on 2026-12-01. Check ai-client.ts and the match-teams HTTP URL for 2.0 model names.

3. Sampling parameters temperature, top_p, top_k deprecated for Gemini 3.6+ models (field-removed, effective 2026-07-21)
   Source: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/changelog.md.txt
   Quote: The sampling parameters `temperature`, `top_p` and `top_k` are now deprecated.
   Affects: fields: temperature, top_p, top_k
   Call sites: lib/ai-client.ts:87 (Passes generationConfig, which may include temperature, topP or topK. These are deprecated for Gemini 3.6+ models.); app/api/hackathon/match-teams/route.ts:135 (The raw HTTP request body may set generationConfig temperature, topP or topK. The body was not read, so this is uncertain.)
   Why it applies: The change only matters if the request sets temperature, top_p or top_k and runs on a Gemini 3.6+ model. The scan shows generationConfig at ai-client.ts but not its contents. Check both sites for sampling params. If the model is being replaced, as in the gemini-2.0-flash shutdown task, drop these params for any 3.6+ target. Otherwise nothing breaks today.

4. Generate Content API: new paid-tier projects now store requests by default (store=true); opt out with store=false (other, effective 2026-10-26)
   Source: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/changelog.md.txt
   Quote: now store requests by default (`store=true`), matching the Interactions API.
   Affects: operations: generateContent, streamGenerateContent, batchGenerateContent; fields: store
   Call sites: app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:56 (The model is used for generateContent, and chat prompts and responses could be stored by default on a new paid-tier project.); lib/ai-advanced-utils.ts:4 (generateContent calls, so the store default applies.); lib/ai-client.ts:87 (generateContent calls, so the store default applies.); lib/ai-utils.ts:4 (generateContent calls, so the store default applies.); app/api/hackathon/match-teams/route.ts:135 (A raw HTTP request, probably generateContent, where store=false can be set explicitly in the request body.)
   Why it applies: The repo calls generateContent through the old SDK and raw HTTP. For new paid-tier projects, requests will be stored by default (store=true). This is a data-retention change, not a break. The code does not set store and handles user chat content. Check whether the project is a new paid-tier one. If privacy requires it, set store=false. The old SDK may not expose the field, so this is easiest to do after the @google/genai migration or on the HTTP call.

5. gemini-2.5-flash deprecated; from Dec 1 2026 requests route to gemini-3.5-flash-lite with breaking API changes (model-retirement, effective 2026-12-01)
   Source: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deprecations.md.txt
   Quote: Effective December 1, 2026, all API requests to `gemini-2.5-flash` will automatically route to
   Affects: operations: gemini-2.5-flash, gemini-3.5-flash-lite; fields: thinking_budget, thinking_level
   Call sites: lib/ai-client.ts:87 (The model is unresolved and may be gemini-2.5-flash. If so, requests will be rerouted to gemini-3.5-flash-lite, with different thinking and sampling behavior.); app/api/hackathon/match-teams/route.ts:135 (The runtime-built URL and body may name gemini-2.5-flash. The model is unknown, so check it.)
   Why it applies: Other call sites use gemini-2.0-flash, but ai-client.ts and the match-teams HTTP call have no resolved model. If either names gemini-2.5-flash, it will be silently rerouted on 2026-12-01 with breaking changes such as thinking_budget versus thinking_level. If neither uses it, close this as no-op. Also make sure the gemini-2.0-flash replacement does not land on gemini-2.5-flash.

6. gemini-2.5-pro deprecated; from Dec 1 2026 requests route to gemini-3.8-flash with breaking API changes (thought_signature validation, thinking_level replaces thinking_budget, sampling params and prefill removed) (model-retirement, effective 2026-12-01)
   Source: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/changelog.md.txt
   Quote: Effective December 1, 2026, all API requests to `gemini-2.5-pro` will automatically route to
   Affects: operations: gemini-2.5-pro, gemini-3.8-flash; fields: thinking_budget, thinking_level, temperature, top_p, top_k
   Call sites: lib/ai-client.ts:87 (The model is unresolved and may be gemini-2.5-pro. If so, requests will be rerouted to gemini-3.8-flash with stricter parameter handling.); app/api/hackathon/match-teams/route.ts:135 (The runtime-built URL and body may name gemini-2.5-pro. The model is unknown, so check it.)
   Why it applies: The scan did not resolve the model at ai-client.ts or in the match-teams HTTP call. If either uses gemini-2.5-pro, it will be automatically rerouted to gemini-3.8-flash on 2026-12-01. The reroute drops sampling parameters and prefill and replaces thinking_budget with thinking_level. The migration agent should check the model and generationConfig there. If neither site uses 2.5-pro, nothing changes.

record.prBody:
## 6 changes: @google/generative-ai (npm) is deprecated and reaches end of life; migrate to @google/genai and more [Verified]

### Change

Replaced @google/generative-ai with @google/genai ^2 (2.32.0) via pnpm. Ported chat route, lib/ai-client.ts, lib/ai-utils.ts and lib/ai-advanced-utils.ts to ai.models.generateContent and result.text. In ai-client.ts, generationConfig moved to config. Replaced gemini-2.0-flash with gemini-2.5-flash-lite everywhere, including the model list in match-teams. Added scripts/check-genai-migration.mjs as the proof test. Typecheck and build pass.

Files touched:
- `app/api/ai/chat/route.ts`
- `app/api/hackathon/match-teams/route.ts`
- `lib/ai-advanced-utils.ts`
- `lib/ai-client.ts`
- `lib/ai-utils.ts`
- `package.json`
- `pnpm-lock.yaml`
- `scripts/check-genai-migration.mjs`

### Why

The old SDK is end of life, and gemini-2.0-flash is shut down.

> All support for this repository (including bug fixes) will permanently end on **November 30, 2025**.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/generative-ai-js/HEAD/README.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | pass | pass | 0 |
| build | pass | pass | 0 |
| genai-proof | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- genai-proof, added by the agent: `export DATABASE_URL='postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/buddy_connect' JWT_SECRET='placeholder-secret-for-build' NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL='http://localhost:3000'; node scripts/check-genai-migration.mjs` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Prepared before the baseline:
- Before the baseline the harness ran `npx prisma generate` (Install scripts were off, so the Prisma client was never generated; @prisma/client imports and the tsc typecheck and next build need it.); it exited 0.
- Checks ran with placeholder env: DATABASE_URL, JWT_SECRET, NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL.

Test of this change: `genai-proof`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- No live call was made, so gemini-2.5-flash-lite behaviour and the API's acceptance of the config are unconfirmed.
- The match-teams route still calls the legacy :generate REST endpoint and the @google-ai/generativelanguage SDK, with 1.5 model ids that are also retired. I only swapped the 2.0 id there. That path needs a separate port to generateContent.
- store=false was not added. This is the Oct 2026 default-storage change. @google/genai 2.32 types config.store, so it can be added at each call site if the project is a new paid-tier one.
- The 3.6+ sampling-parameter deprecation was not applied. ai-client.ts only sends temperature if the caller passes it. The new model is 2.5, so nothing was removed.
- Nothing was changed for the gemini-2.5-flash or gemini-2.5-pro reroutes (changes 5 and 6). The repo's models are 2.0 and 1.5, and the replacement is gemini-2.5-flash-lite, which is not on the deprecation list.
- @google/genai 2.x needs Node >=20. I did not check CI or engines.
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- The default model changed from gemini-2.0-flash to gemini-2.5-flash-lite, so output quality, latency and cost may differ.
- Empty or blocked responses now give an empty string instead of making text() throw. Downstream parsing falls through to its own no-JSON path. ai-client.ts still throws on empty text.
- gemini-2.5-flash-lite is a thinking-capable model, so a small maxOutputTokens could truncate answers.

---

preparation.reasoning: Prisma 7 with prisma-client-js needs `prisma generate` before types exist. The schema has no datasource url, so a prisma.config.ts probably supplies it from DATABASE_URL, and the placeholder lets generate and the build load. JWT_SECRET is likely read at module load, so a placeholder avoids an import-time throw. next build ignores TS errors, but tsc still needs the generated client.

review.summary: The four SDK call sites (chat route, ai-client, ai-utils, ai-advanced-utils) are migrated consistently to `ai.models.generateContent` with `result.text`, and typecheck and build pass. The generated-text shape and the `config` mapping in ai-client look right, but I could not confirm the `@google/genai` ^2.32.0 version from memory; check it against the lockfile and the SDK types. Three things weaken the 'verified' grade. First, the fifth call site (match-teams) is a REST/legacy-SDK path that was only touched by a model-name swap, so the real fix is not made there. Second, the model changed everywhere from gemini-2.0-flash to gemini-2.5-flash-lite, which is more than the SDK migration forces and changes output quality. Third, the 'genai-proof' check is a custom regex script that proves only that strings are present or absent, not that any live call works. Pre-existing, not a concern: match-teams uses a `:generate` REST endpoint with the old `prompt: {text}` shape, which looks like a PaLM-era endpoint that probably never worked with Gemini and falls through to the OpenAI gateway.

concerns.issue: Only the first model string was changed. The route still goes through the `@google-ai/generativelanguage` client and a v1 `:generate` REST URL with a PaLM-style body. The named call site (the runtime-built URL) is not migrated to the new SDK or to `generateContent`. Swapping the model name there likely changes nothing, because that path probably fails and falls through to the `openai/gpt-4-turbo` gateway. The grade's claim of handling every call site is overstated.

The default model was changed to gemini-2.5-flash-lite, a different and smaller model than before. This is a behaviour and quality change not forced by the SDK move. The AbortController timeout is still never wired to the request, so `timeoutMs` has no effect (pre-existing), though the new SDK would support `config.abortSignal`.

Every Gemini call across the app now uses gemini-2.5-flash-lite, chosen by the agent. Output quality, JSON-formatting reliability and cost may differ, and the regex-based JSON parsing is sensitive to this. Nothing tests the new model's outputs. The model could instead be made configurable via an env var.

The 'genai-proof' check is a grep-style script written by the agent. It strips only whole-line `//` comments and checks for string patterns. It cannot show runtime correctness, and it does not cover match-teams. Passing it is weak evidence for a 'verified' grade, as no live API call or mocked test was run.

`@google/genai` ^2.32.0 requires Node >=20 (`engines`), which matches the repo's `>=20.11.0`. I could not confirm from memory that version 2.x exists, so verify it against the registry and the lockfile. The new transitive dependencies (google-auth-library, ws, protobufjs) increase install size.

`result.text ?? ""` silently returns an empty message with success:true when the model returns no text (for example when safety-blocked). Before, `.text()` would throw and produce a 500. This is a small behaviour change in error handling.

checkFirst: Confirm @google/genai ^2.32.0 exists on npm and that `ai.models.generateContent({model, contents, config})` and `response.text` match its types.
Make one live call per migrated module, with a real AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY, to confirm gemini-2.5-flash-lite is available on that key and returns parseable JSON.
Decide whether match-teams should be migrated to `@google/genai` instead of just renaming the model, and test that route's fallback.
Decide whether the model switch to 2.5-flash-lite is intended, or whether it should be an env-configurable setting.
Check how callers handle the empty-string case now returned by chat, ai-utils and ai-advanced-utils.
